9,990 steps at 11:50 PM and you're still pacing your bedroom. What walking 10,000 steps a day for a year really does to you.
Month one, the weighing scale barely moves. But you walk after dinner, take calls on foot, skip the lift, and your bad days start feeling less bad.
By the end of the year, one part of you has actually grown. It's not your legs. Full story on YouTube.
Would you walk every day for a year? Tell me in the comments.

short:
Walking 10,000 steps a day for a year won't fix your weight, and the reason is your own body.
On paper, a year of 10,000 steps a day burns enough calories for almost 10 kilos of weight loss. Real walking studies find people lose far less.
Scientists who studied hunter-gatherers in Tanzania found they burn about the same calories a day as office workers. And the 10,000 goal? It started as a 1960s pedometer name.
Full story on YouTube, with the one thing walking really does change.
